eyebrow: Lesson 18 · B1 · Good Manners with Family · 20 câu
heading: Privacy and Family Dinners
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners with Family – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 8–11.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners with Family (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Your bedroom is a {private|private} place. It holds your own things, and there may be some, like a diary, that you don't want anyone else to see. Other people in your family feel the same way about their rooms, so respect their {privacy|privacy}. Don't look in their chests of drawers or {wardrobes|wardrobes}, and never take anything unless they say it's OK.

paras.label: B
paras.text: If a door is closed, knock before you go in. Say who you are: "It's Michael. May I come in?" Then wait until the person says you can enter. If it is the bathroom, make sure it is empty before you open the door!

paras.label: C
paras.text: A family dinner is a time when everyone gets together to share a meal and talk about their day. But it is not like eating in a restaurant, where someone else does all the work. At home, you need to {pitch in|pitch in}. Offer to help with something simple, like {tearing|tearing} lettuce for a salad. Help {lay the table|lay the table}, clear it afterwards and offer to help wash the dishes.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Making a meal is hard work, so always thank the cook. It doesn't matter if you didn't like the Brussels {sprouts|sprouts}. Mum or Dad did their best to make a {healthy|healthy} meal for the whole family.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Table manners {vary|vary} from country to country. In Brazil, it is rude to leave food on your plate, but in Egypt, leaving a little food is considered polite.

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that tells you exactly what to say outside a closed door
items.why: Đoạn B: *It's Michael. May I come in?*

items.label: A paragraph that mentions something you might want to keep secret
A paragraph that compares a family meal with eating out
items.why: Đoạn C: *not like eating in a restaurant.*

items.label: A paragraph that gives two opposite customs
items.why: Đoạn E: Brazil và Ai Cập trái ngược nhau.

items.label: A paragraph that mentions a vegetable some people dislike

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: Why does the writer mention a diary in (A)?
options: as an example of something people want to keep private
to suggest that everyone should keep a diary
to show how to write about your family
questions.why: Nhật ký là ví dụ cho đồ riêng tư.

questions.q: You may take things from your sister's room if she is not at home.
questions.why: Sai. *never take anything unless they say it's OK.*

questions.q: After knocking on a closed door, what should you do?
options: Wait until the person says you can come in.
questions.why: *wait until the person says you can enter.*

questions.q: According to (C), how is a family dinner different from eating in a restaurant?
options: At home, the food is always healthier.
In a restaurant, you must talk about your day.
In a restaurant, you clear the table yourself.
questions.why: *At home, you need to pitch in.*

questions.q: The writer says you should only thank the cook if you liked the food.
questions.why: Sai. *It doesn't matter if you didn't like the Brussels sprouts.*

questions.q: In which country is leaving a little food on your plate polite?
questions.why: *in Egypt, leaving a little food is considered polite.*

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

options: knocking and asking before he goes in
questions.why: Đoạn B: gõ cửa, xưng tên, xin phép.
questions.alt: A boy knocks on a closed bedroom door and says: It's Michael. May I come in? A girl peeps out from behind the door.

questions.q: Which paragraph does this picture match best?
questions.why: Đoạn C: *offer to help wash the dishes.*
questions.alt: A girl stands next to her mother at the kitchen sink and asks: May I help wash the dishes?

questions.q: Which phrase from the text describes what the girl is doing?
questions.alt: A girl stands next to her mother at the kitchen sink and asks: May I help wash the dishes?

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Every Sunday, my grandma cooks a big dinner for the whole family. [1] This week, she made fish soup, which I don't really like. [2] After dinner, I helped my cousin clear the table. [3]
options: We always go to a restaurant on Sundays so that nobody has to cook.
I usually help by laying the table and tearing lettuce for the salad.
Grandma had forgotten to buy any food that day.
I still ate some and told her it was kind of her to cook for us all.
Then I gave Grandma a hug and thanked her for the meal.

items.why: Giới thiệu việc mình hay phụ giúp.
Không thích món ăn nhưng vẫn lịch sự (ý đoạn D).

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *At home, you need to pitch in* (C). To **pitch in** means to…
*Help lay the table* (C). To **lay the table** means to…
options: put plates, cutlery and glasses on it

questions.q: *Table manners vary from country to country* (E). **Vary** means…
